title: Lesson 4: How Individual Attitudes Affect Team Performance
summary: Professional skills matter, but attitude shapes communication, cooperation, correction, reliability, client experience and growth.

items.label: Focus
items.body: Attitude, behaviour, accountability and team performance

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: Imagine two employees who have the same qualifications, receive the same training and perform similar responsibilities.
The first employee is respectful, punctual, cooperative and willing to learn. When corrected, she listens and makes improvements. When a colleague needs assistance, she helps when possible.
The second employee is frequently defensive, complains about colleagues, resists instructions and becomes irritated whenever something does not go her way.
Although both employees may possess the same technical skills, their attitudes can produce very different results.
The first employee is more likely to strengthen the team, while the second may create unnecessary tension, reduce cooperation and affect the quality of service.
At Zura Spa, professional skills are important, but the attitude with which employees perform their duties also matters.
A skilled employee with an uncooperative attitude can negatively affect colleagues, clients and the organisation.

sections.title: 2. What is attitude?
paragraphs: Attitude is a person's general way of thinking, feeling and responding toward people, situations, responsibilities and experiences.
In the workplace, attitude influences how employees approach their duties, communicate with colleagues, respond to instructions and handle challenges.
Attitude is not always directly visible. However, it often becomes noticeable through behaviour.
For example, an employee may feel frustrated after receiving a correction. Feeling frustrated does not automatically mean the employee has a bad attitude.
What matters is how the employee responds.
She can listen respectfully, ask questions and make improvements, or she can react with hostility and refuse to cooperate.
The goal of professional development is not to eliminate emotions but to help employees manage their responses appropriately.

sections.title: 3. Understanding positive and negative workplace attitudes
paragraphs: A positive attitude does not mean smiling all the time, agreeing with everyone or pretending that problems do not exist.
It means approaching responsibilities and relationships with professionalism, respect and a willingness to contribute constructively.

sections.title: Positive attitudes
list: Respectfulness
Willingness to learn
Cooperation
Accountability
Honesty
Patience
Open-mindedness
Professionalism

sections.title: Negative attitudes
list: Disrespect
Unwillingness to improve
Uncooperativeness
Blame-shifting
Dishonesty
Unnecessary hostility
Dismissiveness
Persistent irresponsibility

sections.title: 4. How individual attitudes affect team performance
A. Attitude affects communication
paragraphs: Employees with respectful attitudes are more likely to communicate clearly, listen to colleagues and discuss concerns constructively.
Employees who frequently respond with hostility, sarcasm or dismissiveness may discourage others from communicating with them.
Zura example: A receptionist informs a therapist that a client has requested a change in appointment time.
A cooperative therapist acknowledges the information and discusses what is possible.
An uncooperative therapist responds rudely, creating tension and making future communication more difficult.
Lesson: The way we respond to information can either encourage or discourage communication.

sections.title: B. Attitude affects cooperation
paragraphs: Teamwork requires employees to recognise that their responsibilities are connected.
An employee who believes that helping colleagues is beneath her may be unwilling to offer reasonable assistance.
An employee with a cooperative attitude understands that appropriate support can improve overall performance.

Zura example: During a busy shift, a therapist notices that another treatment room needs preparation. She has completed her immediate responsibilities and has time to help. Offering assistance may prevent delays and improve the client's experience.
Lesson: Cooperation strengthens team performance, but it should not become an excuse for others to neglect their responsibilities.

sections.title: C. Attitude affects the working environment
paragraphs: The way employees treat one another influences the atmosphere of the workplace.
Respectful behaviour helps create an environment where employees feel comfortable communicating, learning and asking for assistance.
Frequent insults, gossip, intimidation or unnecessary arguments can make the workplace stressful and reduce trust.
Lesson: Every employee contributes to the atmosphere of the workplace through everyday behaviour.

sections.title: D. Attitude affects how employees receive correction
paragraphs: No employee performs perfectly all the time. Mistakes, misunderstandings and areas requiring improvement are normal parts of work.
What matters is how employees respond when these issues are identified.
A professional employee listens to feedback, seeks clarification when necessary and makes reasonable improvements.
An employee who automatically treats every correction as a personal attack may struggle to improve.
Zura example: A supervisor notices that a treatment room was not prepared according to the required standard.
Unconstructive response: "Why are you always complaining about my work? Other people do the same thing."
Constructive response: "Thank you for pointing it out. Please clarify what needs to be corrected so I can meet the standard."
Employees should also be able to question feedback respectfully when they believe it is inaccurate or unfair.
Lesson: Receiving correction professionally does not mean accepting unfair treatment. It means addressing feedback constructively.

sections.title: E. Attitude affects reliability and accountability
paragraphs: An employee's attitude toward responsibility can influence punctuality, attention to detail, honesty and willingness to report mistakes.
Employees who take their duties seriously help colleagues plan and work confidently.
Repeated irresponsibility can create additional work for others and reduce trust.
Lesson: Reliability is demonstrated through consistent actions, not promises alone.

sections.title: F. Attitude affects client satisfaction
paragraphs: Clients may notice the way employees communicate, respond to requests and manage their responsibilities.
A therapist may possess excellent massage skills, but dismissive or disrespectful behaviour can still damage the client's experience.
Similarly, a receptionist who communicates politely and resolves issues professionally can help clients feel valued.
Lesson: Professional attitude is part of the service Zura Spa provides.

sections.title: G. Attitude affects employee growth
paragraphs: Employees who remain open to learning are more likely to develop new skills, improve their performance and take on additional responsibilities.
Employees who consistently reject feedback or believe they have nothing left to learn may limit their development.
Lesson: A willingness to learn is an important part of professional growth.

sections.title: 5. How one person's attitude can influence the entire team
paragraphs: Attitudes are personal, but their effects can extend beyond the individual.
This is an illustrative example of how repeated behaviour can affect team performance, not an inevitable outcome.
The reverse can also happen. An employee who consistently communicates respectfully, supports colleagues and takes responsibility can encourage similar behaviour in others.
Every employee has the ability to influence the team's working culture through daily actions.

sections.title: The impact of repeated disrespectful behaviour
list: An employee frequently responds rudely to colleagues.
Colleagues become reluctant to communicate with her.
Important information may be delayed or withheld.
Coordination and service quality may suffer.

sections.title: 6. Eight attitudes every Zura employee should develop

items.label: 1. Respect
items.body: Treat every colleague with dignity, regardless of role, experience or personal differences.

items.label: 2. Willingness to learn
items.body: Be open to instructions, new ideas, constructive feedback and professional development.

items.label: 3. Cooperation
items.body: Work constructively with colleagues and offer reasonable assistance when needed.

items.label: 4. Accountability
items.body: Accept responsibility for your decisions, actions and assigned duties.

items.label: 5. Honesty
items.body: Communicate truthfully, acknowledge mistakes and avoid concealing important problems.

items.label: 6. Emotional maturity
items.body: Manage frustration, avoid impulsive reactions and respond thoughtfully during disagreements.

items.label: 7. Reliability
items.body: Be punctual, fulfil commitments and communicate promptly when something affects your work.

items.label: 8. Commitment to improvement
items.body: Look for opportunities to become more effective, professional and supportive.

sections.title: Case study 1: The employee who dislikes correction
paragraphs: A therapist has been reminded several times to prepare her treatment room before clients arrive.
Whenever the supervisor raises the issue, she becomes defensive and complains that management is picking on her.
Other therapists begin avoiding discussions about room preparation because they do not want arguments.
Expected lesson: Employees should respond to correction constructively, while supervisors should provide clear, fair and respectful feedback.
list: How might this employee's attitude affect the team?
What would be a more professional response to correction?
What should the supervisor do if the behaviour continues?
How can the team address the issue without gossiping about the employee?

sections.title: Case study 2: The employee who spreads negativity
paragraphs: A staff member frequently complains about colleagues behind their backs.
She makes negative comments about their abilities and encourages others to take sides during disagreements.
Over time, some employees become uncomfortable sharing information or working together.
Expected lesson: Workplace concerns should be addressed through constructive conversations and appropriate reporting channels, not gossip or personal attacks.
list: How can gossip affect trust?
What should colleagues do when someone encourages them to speak negatively about another employee?
How should genuine workplace concerns be raised?
What can management do to encourage respectful communication?

sections.title: Case study 3: The employee with a positive attitude
paragraphs: A newly employed therapist is still learning Zura's service standards.
She asks questions when uncertain, listens to feedback and makes corrections when necessary.
When colleagues need reasonable assistance, she offers to help while ensuring her own duties are completed.
Expected lesson: Professionalism is demonstrated through consistent behaviour, accountability and willingness to improve.
list: What attitudes is this employee demonstrating?
How might her behaviour influence colleagues?
Why is willingness to learn valuable?
How can management encourage similar behaviour across the team?

sections.title: 8. Practical exercise: Choose your response
paragraphs: Complete the Workplace Attitude Exercise at the bottom of this lesson. Choose how you would respond to each situation, give your reason, then submit.
list: Your supervisor points out a mistake in your work. Explain why everyone else also makes mistakes / Listen, seek clarification and correct the issue / Ignore the feedback because you disagree.

A colleague receives praise from management for excellent performance. Congratulate her and learn from her strengths / Dismiss her achievement as favouritism without evidence / Stop cooperating with her because she is receiving attention.

You are frustrated by a colleague's behaviour. Discuss the issue with other staff to gather support / Respond angrily to make your feelings clear / Address the issue calmly or raise it through the appropriate channel.

You notice a colleague struggling with an unfamiliar procedure. Offer guidance if you are able and authorised to do so / Mock her for not knowing what to do / Ignore her because she should already know.

sections.title: 9. Personal attitude assessment
paragraphs: Employees should reflect on their own behaviour rather than evaluating or criticising colleagues.
Rate yourself honestly: 1 = Rarely, 2 = Sometimes, 3 = Often, 4 = Consistently.
list: I communicate respectfully, even when I disagree.
I accept constructive feedback and make improvements.
I take responsibility for my mistakes.
I offer reasonable assistance to colleagues.
I avoid gossip and unnecessary arguments.
I manage frustration without treating others disrespectfully.
I fulfil my commitments and communicate delays.
I am willing to learn from colleagues and supervisors.

sections.title: 10. Personal assignment
paragraphs: Each employee should provide written answers to the following questions:
list: In your own words, explain what attitude means in the workplace.
Identify five positive attitudes that contribute to effective teamwork.
Explain three ways one employee's negative behaviour can affect colleagues and clients.
Describe a situation where you responded poorly to a workplace issue. How could you have handled it differently?
Identify two personal attitudes you want to improve and explain the practical steps you will take.
Explain how your attitude toward correction can affect your professional development.

sections.title: 11. Daily attitude improvement challenge
paragraphs: For the next seven working days, each staff member should deliberately practise one positive workplace behaviour every day.
The purpose is to encourage consistent habits rather than temporary behaviour during training.
table: Offer reasonable assistance to someone who needs it
Take responsibility for a task without repeated reminders
Avoid gossip and redirect negative conversations constructively
Demonstrate patience during a challenging situation
Reflect on improvements and identify the next area for growth

sections.title: 12. Final lesson and takeaway
paragraphs: Every employee brings personal attitudes into the workplace. Those attitudes influence communication, cooperation, trust, service quality and overall team performance.
Professionalism does not require employees to be happy all the time or to suppress legitimate concerns.
It requires them to take responsibility for how they behave, treat others respectfully and remain committed to improvement.
At Zura Spa, employees should be recognised not only for technical competence but also for their reliability, cooperation, accountability and contribution to a healthy workplace.
Next topic: Putting Team Success Above Personal Ego.

remember: Your attitude is personal, but its impact is shared. The way you treat colleagues, respond to responsibilities and handle challenges can either strengthen or weaken the entire team.
